title: Sad But Relieved Face Emoji 😥: Is That Sweat or a Tear?
description: The 😥 sad but relieved face emoji shows a sweat drop, not a tear. It means a close call, weary disappointment or “phew, that was rough.” Examples inside.
summary: The 😥 sad but relieved face has furrowed brows, a small frown and a single drop on its forehead. Officially it shows mixed feelings: disappointed about how something went but relieved it was not worse. Many people read the drop as a tear and use the emoji simply to mean sad or stressed.
meaning: This is one of the most misread emojis. The drop is drawn at the side of the brow, which makes it sweat by the usual cartoon rules, and the character's former Unicode name was “disappointed but relieved face.” The intended feeling is the shaky exhale after a narrow escape: you passed, barely; the car is damaged, but nobody was hurt.

In practice, plenty of senders see a crying face. On small screens the drop sits close enough to the eye that it resembles a tear, so 😥 is widely used for ordinary sadness, sympathy and “I feel bad about this.” Neither group is wrong, exactly; the emoji now carries both meanings, and the words around it show which one applies.

It also covers plain weariness and strain. Someone who has been dealing with a sick child all night or a week of overtime might send 😥 to say they are worn down and worried. In that sense it overlaps with 😓, though 😥 keeps its eyes open and looks more concerned than defeated.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Close calls are its home turf: “thought I lost my wallet, it was in the car 😥.” It also softens disappointing news, such as not getting tickets or having to cancel plans, by showing the sender feels bad about it. Because readers split between “sad” and “relieved,” add a few words if the difference matters.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: Commenters use it to express sympathy under posts about illness, lost pets and hard times, treating it as a gentle crying face. Sports fans post it after a scrappy win that should have been easier, which is closer to the original mixed-feelings meaning.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It fits a message like “that client call was tough, but we kept the account 😥.” It acknowledges stress without drama. Avoid using it when delivering bad news to someone who reports to you, since it centers your discomfort instead of theirs.

examples.text: Passed the exam by two points 😥
examples.meaning: Relieved to have scraped through, and still rattled by how close it was.

examples.text: Sorry I can't make it Saturday 😥
examples.meaning: The sender feels bad about letting someone down.

examples.text: The storm missed us but the neighbors lost their fence 😥
examples.meaning: Grateful to be fine and sorry for others who were not.

examples.text: Been at the ER since 3am. He's okay now 😥
examples.meaning: Exhausted and worried, with relief finally arriving.

examples.text: We won but that was painful to watch 😥
examples.meaning: Happy with the result and unhappy with how it happened.

combos.meaning: Shaken but thankful that things turned out all right.
Sad and hurting; here the drop is being read as a tear.
A stressful episode followed by a long sigh of relief.

confusedWith.difference: 😢 has a tear falling from the eye onto the cheek and means sadness. The drop on 😥 is on the forehead and is meant as sweat, giving it a stressed, relieved-but-shaken tone.
😅 smiles broadly and laughs off an awkward moment or near miss. 😥 frowns; the danger has passed, but the sender is not laughing about it.
😰 has a blue forehead and open mouth, showing anxiety that is still going on. 😥 is calmer and all yellow, as if the worst is already over.

avoid: Do not rely on it alone to express condolences, because some readers will see relief in it.
Avoid it when you want to show unambiguous happiness about good news.
If you mean you are crying, 😢 or 😭 remove the guesswork.
design: A yellow face with eyebrows drawn together, open eyes, a small frown and one blue droplet beside the forehead. The position of the drop is what causes confusion: it is placed high, by the brow, to indicate sweat, yet close enough to the eye on some platforms to pass for a tear. The overall look is otherwise consistent across vendors.

faqs.a: Sweating, by design. The drop sits on the forehead, and the emoji was created to show disappointment mixed with relief. That said, many people use it as a mild crying face, and that reading is common enough to be understood.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 😥 and 😢?
faqs.a: 😢 is straightforward sadness, with a tear on the cheek. 😥 is more complicated: stressed, worn out or relieved after something difficult. If you want sympathy for a loss, 😢 is clearer.

faqs.q: What does 😥 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: There is no gendered meaning. The person is usually telling you they feel bad about something, are stressed, or just got through a tense situation. Look at the message it is attached to for which one applies.

faqs.q: Why is it called sad but relieved?
faqs.a: The name describes two feelings at once: unhappiness over what happened and relief that it is finished or was not worse. Its earlier name, “disappointed but relieved face,” said the same thing.
